30.08.2023 (Clause 31) AWARD 1.

As per the facts of the present case, on 16.03.2015, at about 8.00 A.M the deceased Sunil Malik S/O Sh Abhimannu , was going on main Gurgaon Road, near PNB,Deenpur Najafgarh, New Delhi on his motor cycle bearing No. DL 4SBSO0191 on a correct side of the road.
Meanwhile a car bearing No. DLIT AQ9640, which was being driven by its driver came at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and hit the motor cycle of deceased with great force.
As a result of which deceased fell down on the road and received grievous injuries.

He was immediately taken to Chayan Hospital Delhi but after first aid he was referred to Ayushman Hospital, Dwarka , Delhi for his treatment but during the course of treatment, he (deceased) expired on 21.03.2025.
2. It is contended that the said accident took place, due to rash and negligent driving of Vikash, who has been impleaded as respondent no. 1.
The owner of offending vehicle, Sh Rajiv Kumar , is impleaded as respondent no. 2.
And as the said vehicle was insured with National Insurance Company Ltd., it is impleaded as respondent no. 3 in the present case.
By the present case, the petitioners are claiming a sum of Rs. 33,65,000/ (Rupees Thirty Three Lacs and Sixty Five Thousand Only) from respondents as compensation.
3. The respondent No.1 has filed his W.S stating therein that the accident was caused due to gross mistake of the deceased himself
4. The respondent No.2 has filed his WS stating therein that there is no casuse of action arise against the respondents as petitioners have filed a vague case against the respondents.

5. The respondent no. 3 (insurance company) has filed its written statement stating therein that the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner as there is violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy as the offending vehicle was not having a valid permit at the time of accident.

6. After completion of the proceedings, following issues were framed on 21.03.2016 as under:
(i) Whether Sunil Malik S/O Sh Abhimannu @ Abhay Ram sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated 16.03.2015 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle ( Car) No. DL1T AQ 9640 being driven by Respondent 1 Vikash and owned by Respondent No.2 / Rajiv Kumar and insured by respondent No.3 / National Insurance Company Ltd ?

OPP. 
(ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to claim compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?

OPP.

5 (iii) Relief.
7. In order to prove their claim, petitioner have examined petitioner No.1 Sh Abhimannu as PW1.
Sh Ajay Kumar Shokeen, as PW2 and Sh Mehar Singh,as an eye witness, as PW3.
The respondent No.2 has examined Sh Sandeep Prasad, Transport Inspector RTA Gurugram as R2W1 and Respondent No.3 has examined Sh B.S Yadav, Assistant as R3W1.
8. I have heard ld. Counsel for the petitioner as well as Ld Counsel for the R.2 and R.3,Insurance company.
None has appeared on behalf of R.1.I have given my thoughtful consideration to the submission made by them and I also perused the record.

My issuewise findings are as under:
(i) Whether Sunil Malik S/O Sh Abhimannu @ Abhay Ram sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated 16.03.2015 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle ( Car) No. DL1T AQ 9640 being driven by Respondent 1 Vikash and owned by Respondent No.2 / Rajiv Kumar and insured by respondent No.3 / National Insurance Company Ltd ? OPP.
9.
In order to prove this issue, petitioners have examined PW 3 Sh Mehar Singh, an eye witness.

He has deposed that on 16.03.2015 at about 8.00 p.m, he was waiting on the main road of his house when he saw that one motorcyclist was hit by a Swift Dezire Car due to this impact, the motorcyclist fell down on the road and driver of said car run away from the spot.
He has deposed that he took lift from a car and chased the offending vehicle and same was stopped and caught near Hero Honda Showroom at Roshanpura Main Road.
He has deposed that the name of the driver was revealed as Vikash.
The driver of the offending was brought to the spot and injured was taken to Chayan Hospital, Deenpur by him.
He has deposed that after first aid he was removed to Ayushman Hospital.
Sector12, Dwarka N Delhi
. He has deposed that accident was caused due to high speed and in a rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
The aforesaid witness has been duly cross examined by respondent No.2 and 3 but the testimony of this witness could not be impeached.
Moreover the proof of negligence, while disposing of a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/304A of IPC.
The allegations levelled in the written statement howsoever strong that may be, cannot take place of proof.
Therefore, the evidence which has come on the file only can be considered.
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that deceased was at fault , in any way while driving his motorcycle.
10. The fact that Sunil Malik died in that accident is also supported by his postmortem report on the dead body of victim.

Considering all the evidence as discussed above, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent No.1 thereby causing death of Sunil Malik .
11.

This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that victim Sunil Malik died in a motor vehicle accident due to rash negligent driving by respondent no.1.
ISSUE No.2: Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?

OPP.

6 12.
It is not disputed during arguments that petitioners are the father and mother of victim.
Moreover, this fact is established by statement of Sh Abhimannu (PW1) father of deceased that petitioner No.1 and 2 are father and mother of deceased.
Being LRs of deceased, petitioners are well within their rights to claim compensation from respondents.
13. Now coming to the extent of compensation.

According to the petitioner, at the time of accident,
the deceased Sunil Malik was working as milk vendor and was earning Rs.30,000/ to 50,000/
p.m.
But no documentary evidence is being produced by the petitioner to substantiate the income of the deceased.
Moreover PW2 Ajay Shokeen who has deposed that deceased used to take approximately 100 liter milk from him has also not produced any document to substantiate his deposition.
No record being maintained in due course of business as sale and purchase record of milk by deceased produced on judicial file.
However,Ld Counsel for the petitioner has conceded to the fact and submitted that the income of the deceased may be assessed as per Minimum Wages Act.
As per examination certificate Ex PW1/3 ( Colly) the deceased was matriculate from Board of School Education Haryana.
So this Tribunal has assessed the monthly income of deceased as 10,478/ pm for computation of compensation as per Minimum Wages of Matriculates prevalent in Delhi at the time of accident.
14. Keeping in view the fact that the age of the deceased was 22 years old ( As per educational certificate Ex PW1/3) at the time of accident.

And as per the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others of Hon'ble Supreme Court the net income of the deceased is to be counted after deduction of tax and future benefit have to be given @ 40%.

sentences.text: 15. The deceased was Bachelor at the time of accident so ( on the established law by the Hon'ble Superior Courts ) deceased could have spending 50% of his income on his personal expenses.

Therefore the income for the purpose of loss of dependency has to be taken as Rs. 7,334,60/
(10,478/ + 4,191.20/  7334.60/) per month.
16. To calculate loss of dependency, the multiplier has to be taken on the basis of age of deceased.
A multiplier of 18 is thus taken in calculating loss of dependency.
Counting in this way, loss of dependency comes to Rs. 15,84,273.60/ ( 7,334.60/ x 12 x 18).

This amount of Rs.15,85,000/ (
in lumpsum) is allowed to petitioners for loss of dependency.

17. Apart from amount mentioned above, petitioner No.1 is also granted a sum of Rs.17,000/ for funeral expenses, Rs.17,000/ for loss of estate and Rs. 88,000/ (Rs.44,000/ each of the petitioiner) for loss of consortium.

18. Ld Counsel for the petitioners submits that there are medical bills amounting to Rs.3,23,923/
.But

after scrutinized all the bills being filed by the petitioners, the total amount of medical bills comes to Rs.2,98,419/ as an amount of Rs.20,000/ which has been paid on 17.03.2015 as advance has also been added in bill dated 17.03.2015.There is no rebuttal to these medical bills Ex PW1/1 ( Colly).
So this amount of Rs.2,98,419/ is granted to the petitioners towards medical expenses incurred by them.

19 . Now coming to the extent of liability.
It has already been held herein above that the deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
He is primarily liable to make payment.
However, the petitioners have made the respondent no.3 (insurance company) as one of the party seeking direction to respondent no.3 to pay the compensation.
20. The only submission of Ld Counsel for insurance company is that the Insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
It is submitted that respondent No.1 was not possessing any valid permit to drive car, as taxi on the road at the time of accident.
In this regard R3 has examined R3W1 Sh B.S Yadav, who has proved the copy of insurance policy vide Ex R3W1/1.
He has deposed that the offending vehicle was being driven by R.1 in contravention of insurance policy.
He has proved copy of legal notice U/O 12 rule 8 CPC served upon R.1 and R.2 to provide the valid permit of offending vehicle.

On perusal of the record it reveals that the accident in this case took place on 16.03.2015.The registration of offending vehicle was done on 19.03.2015 as Cab Taxi in the name of M/S Fast Track Cabs.
The payment receipt for issuance of permit was issued by the office of RTA Gurugram Haryana on 24.03.2015.
So it is proved on record that respondent No.1 was not having valid permit to drive the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that petitioners are entitled for compensation from respondent no.3, who in turn has a right to recover the same from respondent no.1 and 2 jointly and severally after making payment to the petitioner.
